case_name: Sh. Gaurav Sharma vs Smt.Shipali Sharma
facts_of_case: The wife filed a revision petition against an order dated 23.02.2016, while the husband also filed a revision petition against the same order. The wife alleged that the respondents had failed to appreciate evidence and actively participated in the commission of an offence.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the respondent to prove the second marriage of the petitioner.
legal_principles.held: The burden is on the respondent to prove the second marriage of the petitioner as mere admission of the second marriage of the petitioner is of no consequence.

legal_principles.principle: The period of filing an appeal against the divorce decree is 30 days as provided under the Hindu Marriage Act.
A mere admission of the second marriage of the petitioner is of no consequence.
legal_principles.held: The burden is on the respondent to prove the second marriage of the petitioner as mere admission of the second marriage of the petitioner is of no consequence.

legal_principles.principle: The petitioner has not committed any offence U/s 494 IPC after taking divorce on 11.09.2013.

outcome.final_order: The court decided both revision petitions together, allowing the appeals.
